newsitem.title: GREECE: National Bank says H1 pretax up 94 percent.
newsitem.headline: National Bank says H1 pretax up 94 percent.

text.p: National Bank, Greece's largest commercial bank, said in a statement its half-year pretax profit rose 94 percent on a provision basis to around 33 billion drachmas compared to 17 billion a year earlier.
Loan loss provisions for the first six months of 1997 were 18.1 billion drachmas, up from 7.1 billion in the respective period of 1996, the statement said.
Operating expenses, excluding salaries and taxation, grew 7.4 percent year-on-year in January-June 1997, easing from 15.1 percent in the the first half of 1996, National said.

"The improvement in profitability is linked to our modernisation programme which contributed to an increase in operating profit and a cut back in general expenses," it said. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
